title: How Silver Spring Brick Houses and Urban Dust Load Your Air Ducts
headline: Retrofitted trunks, Georgia Avenue particles, and why older registers film over
description: Silver Spring, MD mixes pre-war brick, downtown construction, and humid basements. Learn why ducts collect urban dust and pollen, and when to clean them from Bethesda.

sections.heading: Silver Spring is urban Montgomery County
paragraphs: Downtown around the Metro, Woodside bungalows, and Georgia Avenue apartments do not look like a quiet suburb. Construction, bus traffic, and the Purple Line corridor put dust in the air. Older brick houses often got central air decades after they were built. Those cut-in trunks have joints that collect whatever the last renovation left behind.
Basements stay cool. Maryland summers stay wet. Cold supply ducts sweat. Urban dust and tree pollen stick to that moisture.

sections.heading: Downtown condos fail on the dryer vent
paragraphs: Stacked units have long, bent dryer runs. Lint packs. Moisture blows back into the laundry closet. That humidity then feeds whatever is already living in the ducts.
If the smell is already there, start with [air duct cleaning in Silver Spring, MD](/locations/silver-spring).

sections.heading: Typical signs in a Silver Spring house
listItems: Musty air in the first minutes after heat or AC turns on.
Black or gray film around supplies a few days after you wipe them.
A dryer that needs two cycles in a downtown building.

faq.q: Why do older Silver Spring houses get musty ducts?
faq.a: Retrofitted metal trunks in cool basements sweat in Maryland humidity. Urban dust and pollen stick to that film and blow back when the system starts.
